chapter_theme: Truthfulness is defined by what speech does rather than by whether it matches facts: speech without harm is truth, and a falsehood yielding faultless good counts as truth. The chapter then raises this virtue above austerity, giving, and every other good.
structure_note: Parimelazhagar divides the chapter: the definition of truth and falsehood (291-292), that falsehood can't be hidden (293), its fruit in this world (294), its fruit beyond (295-297), and its supremacy (298-300).

291.reading: If you ask what truth is, it is speech containing no evil at all.
291.nuance: A surprising definition, because nothing here refers to facts. Parimelazhagar spells out the consequence: stating what happened isn't the definition, and even an accurate report is falsehood if it harms.

positions.position: Reporting what actually occurred is excluded as the definition of truth.

292.reading: Even falsehood is in the place of truth, if it yields good that is free of fault.
292.nuance: புரைதீர்ந்த does the limiting work: this excuses no convenient lie. Parimelazhagar's example is a falsehood that saves a creature from ruin or death, and he builds 291 and 292 into a four-way scheme crossing fact with effect.

positions.position: Truth and falsehood are classified by effect: useful non-fact is truth, and harmful or useless fact is falsehood.
positions.quote: 'தீங்கு பயவாத நிகழ்ந்தது கூறலும், நன்மை பயக்கும் நிகழாதது கூறலும் மெய்ம்மை'

293.reading: Don't lie about what your own heart knows; once you lie, your own heart will burn you.
293.nuance: The harm returns by the same organ of knowing. Parimelazhagar has the heart as a witness that brings on the sin's result, and Manakkudavar has it as remorse on seeing what the lie did to others. Kalaignar's 'conscience' is a modern word for the same thing.

294.reading: If one conducts oneself without being false in one's heart, one lives in the hearts of all the world.
294.nuance: உள்ளம் appears on both sides of the verse: inner truth gives a place in others' inner lives. Parimelazhagar narrows 'the world' to the elevated, and says it is speech that has to match the heart. Manakkudavar and Kalaignar make it not even thinking a lie.

295.reading: If one speaks truth together with one's heart, one is above those who practise austerity along with giving.
295.nuance: Parimelazhagar's reason is about levels of the person: acts of body are outward, but acts of mind and speech are inward. Note that truth is ranked here above the two virtues that chapters 23 and 27 have just exalted.

296.reading: There is no renown like not lying, and it brings all virtue without எய்யாமை.

positions.position: Without bodily strain: it spares the toil that wealth-gathering and fasting demand.
positions.quote: மறுமைக்கு மெய் வருந்தாமல் அவனுக்கு எல்லா அறங்களையும் தானே கொடுக்கும்.

positions.position: Without his knowing: virtue accrues to him unawares.
positions.quote: பொய்யாமையானது அவனறியாமல் தானே எல்லா அறங்களையுங் கொடுக்குமாதலான்,

positions.position: It brings benefits that never leave.
positions.quote: என்றும் நீங்காத அறவழி நலன்களை அளிப்பது அந்த வாழ்வேயாகும்.

297.reading: If one keeps up not lying, not lying, then not doing other virtues, not doing them, is good.
297.nuance: The commentators' opposed readings depend on where the doubled words are divided. Parimelazhagar knows and rejects a reading like Manakkudavar's.

positions.position: Truthfulness alone suffices, and it is better to skip other virtues than to attempt many and fail.
positions.quote: அவன் பிற அறங்களைச் செய்யாமையே செய்யாமையே நன்று.

positions.position: The opposite stress: other virtues are good only if truthfulness is unfailing, and otherwise they turn bad.
positions.quote: பொய்யாமையைப் பொய்யாமல் செலுத்துவனாயின், பிற அறங் களைச் செய்தல் நன்றாம்; அல்லது தீதாம்,

298.reading: Outer purity comes about through water; inner purity is seen through truth.
298.nuance: காணப்படும் is more ambiguous than it looks. Parimelazhagar explains that what is seen exists, so truth produces purity, whereas Manakkudavar says purity is known by truthful speech, which makes truth its evidence. Parimelazhagar also infers that renunciants need both purities.

299.reading: Not all lamps are lamps; for the worthy, the unfailing lamp alone is the lamp.
299.nuance: பொய்யா, 'unfailing' and also 'unlying', makes truth a kind of light that shows things as they are.

positions.position: The rejected lamps are worldly lights such as sun, moon and fire, which dispel outer darkness only.
positions.quote: புறத்து இருள் கடியும் உலகத்தார் விளக்குகள் எல்லாம் விளக்கு ஆகா;

positions.position: விளக்கு is the radiance of a good person, and what is rejected is radiance earned by other virtues.
positions.quote: சான்றோர்க்கு எல்லாவறத்தினாலும் உண்டான ஒளியும் ஒளி யல்ல ;

300.reading: Among the things we have seen as true, there is nothing at all better than truthfulness.
300.nuance: The first person, யாம், is a rare moment when the poet speaks as himself. Parimelazhagar turns 'what we have seen' into the scriptures revealed by the Lord, but Manakkudavar keeps it simple as what we have found to be true, and nothing in the verse mentions texts.

links.note: 300 finds nothing better than truthfulness, while 323 puts not killing first and truthfulness right behind it. The Kural declares its rankings chapter by chapter, and here it comes close to correcting itself.

Almost the same phrase is applied to opposite things: பொய்யா விளக்கு is truthfulness here, and 753 calls wealth the பொய்யா விளக்கம் that cuts through darkness. The section on wealth deliberately takes over the language of the section on virtue.
297 prizes unbroken not-lying, while 292 admits falsehood under a condition. They are consistent only given 291's redefinition of truth by effect, which shows how much that definition is carrying.
225 favours giving over austerity, the commentators on 263 favour austerity over giving, and 295 now sets truth above both. The chapters rank a shifting set of virtues rather than a fixed ladder.
278 shows the bathers with impure minds, and 298 states the principle that this water only reaches the body. Read together, the chapter on hypocrisy provides the case for this general claim.

source_issues: 298: the verse text has புறள்தூய்மை for புறந்தூய்மை.
